column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management

column1: Infectious Substances Shipping Training (e-ISST) Global
column2: Contribute to improving compliance with applicable regulations, ensuring safety of staff, the public and the environment. Compliance also increases access to carrier services, and subsequent timely package delivery.
column3: Laboratory

column2: Learn how to analyse, summarise, report, present, and interpret data collected within a sentinel influenza surveillance system.
column3: Surveillance

column2: Workshop to build capacity in influenza surveillance data analysis, threshold setting and bulletin writing
column3: Surveillance

column2: Review approach and support in application of Pandemic Influenza Severity Assessment and appyling threshold setting to inluenza/syndromic surveillance data using the moving epidemic method
column3: Surveillance

column1: Infodemic Management 101
column2: Course is for anyone interested in understanding what an infodemic is, how it dramatically affects public health and what we can do about it now and into the future
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Infodemic Management: Addressing health misinformation and disinformation
column2: This course introduces the learners to the concept of health misinformation in an infodemic management context, what harms it can cause, how it spreads, and how to prevent and manage it. It also dives deeper into the difference between misinformation and disinformation with an overview of how threat actors weaponize information during public health emergencies to cause harm.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Infodemic Management: Defining a taxonomy for social listening
column2: When practicing social listening activities for public health purposes such as infodemic management, health professionals need a taxonomy adapted to their questions and to the domain they cover. Tailoring their search strategy to collect data relevant for infodemic insights generation will allow them to build strong and evidence-based recommendations for public health action. This course will equip health public health workers to design a taxonomy for social listening adapted to their needs.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Infodemic management: Developing an infodemic insights report
column2: This course, which is part of the “Infodemic management course series” provides an overview of the steps the learners can take to plan for and develop an infodemic insights report. Developing an infodemic insights report is one of the key actions taken by infodemic managers to help health authorities and partners identify, questions, concerns, information voids, narratives and circulating mis- and disinformation on a particular health topic and propose preventive and corrective actions toward mitigating the infodemic.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Infodemic Management: Social marketing and message testing methods
column2: This course shows how social marketing and message testing methods can help public health authorities to design effective campaigns and interventions.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Infodemic Management: Using human-centered design good practices
column2: This course helps public health workers to understand and use best practices of Human-Centered Design (HCD) to inform their work at different stages of their infodemic management process.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Infodemic Management: Working effectively as an infodemic manager in the field
column2: This course introduces learners to the work of an infodemic manager in the field, during health emergencies or in routine. It explains what the principles of this new kind of job are. It also allows learners to discover what tasks and challenges an infodemic manager needs to handle, and how to master them.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Interregional Field Simulation Exercise (IFX) Programme for Rapid Response Mobile Labs
column2: Rapid Response Mobile Laboratories (RRMLs) provide critical laboratory diagnostic support in crisis situations and are an important asset of the global emergency workforce. In 2018, the Health Emergencies Programme (WHE) at the WHO Regional Office for Europe established the RRML Network, driven by the European partner institutions of the Global Outbreak Alert and Response Network (GOARN), to advance and integrate RRMLs into existing preparedness and response structures and to standardize RRML operations in the field.
column3: Laboratory

column1: Introducing Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) in emergencies
column2: Strengthening the competencies of health sector actors working in emergencies, to establish, support and scale up Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in countries.
column3: Health services provision

column1: Introduction to Epidemic Intelligence from Open Sources
column2: This series of videos provides an introduction to the EIOS Initiative and the EIOS System. This course provides an orientation of the key features and functionalities of the EIOS System.
column3: Surveillance
column5: Health care workforce, public healht officers and policy makers/ Member states/ MoH/WHO staff

column1: Introduction to IHR Monitoring and Evaluation
column2: Build M&E capacities necessary to monitor implementation of IHR among member states. * "The training will need to be updated to align with the IHR amendments when they enter into force"
column3: Research & monitoring and evaluation

column2: Overview of the signs, symptoms, transmission routes, diagnosis, and epidemiology of the disease. It also discusses prevention and control strategies.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management

column1: Introduction to Nipah virus disease

column1: Introduction to oxygen systems
column2: The course provides an overview of medical oxygen systems, their ecosystem, life cycle, and global procurement challenges, with a focus on standards and ethical considerations.
column3: Health services provision

column1: Emergency Response Framework (ERF)
column2: The Emergency Response Framework provides WHO staff with essential guidance on how the Organization manages the assessment, grading and response to public health events and emergencies with health consequences, in support of Member States and affected communities. Building on the principles of the ERF, this course provides an overview of WHO’s role in emergencies, the Incident Management System (IMS) and its key functions, and the process from verification to response to a public health emergency.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management

column1: Introduction to the International Health Regulations (IHR)
column2: This course, designed as an evolving scenario-based exercise in a fictional country, aims to equip participants with the knowledge needed to assess public health events and notify them to WHO as required under the International Health Regulations. * "The training will need to be updated to align with the IHR amendments when they enter into force"
column3: IHR Coordination and National IHR Focal Point Functions
column5: "National International Health Regulations Focal Points,WHO IHR Contact Points,  Other IHR stakeholders "

column1: Joint External Evaluation - Team Member Orientation
column2: Describe the key steps of the Joint External Evaluation (JEE) process and the role of team members when facilitating technical discussions and drafting the Final Report
column3: Research & monitoring and evaluation

column1: Joint External Evaluation : Introduction
column2: The course provides understanding of the JEE process, its objectives, principles, and methods. The course will also demonstrate how the JEE results can inform the strengthening of health security capacities and the development and implementation of the National Action Plan for Health Security (NAPHS).
column3: Research & monitoring and evaluation
column5: Country teams, external experts and technical writers

column1: Joint External Evaluation for Subject Matter Experts
column2: This course aims to provide JEE subject matter experts (JEE SMEs) with an understanding of the JEE process, its objectives, principles, and methods. The course provides an in-depth focus on the role of JEE SMEs in conducting an effective evaluation and writing technical area reports.
column3: Research & monitoring and evaluation

column1: Joint External Evaluation for Technical Writers
column2: This course aims to provide technical writers with an understanding of the JEE process, its objectives, principles, and the importance of coming up with a JEE report that reflects the results of the evaluation.
column3: Research & monitoring and evaluation

column5: MoH and WHO (emergencies) staff: Incident Manager, Health Cluster Coordinator and Function Team Leads

column2: This course equips participants with the knowledge and skills to effectively manage mass casualty incidents. It covers key aspects such as preparedness, response, and recovery based on the emergency unit’s mass casualty management plan. Participants will learn how to assign staff roles, coordinate internal and external communication, and ensure smooth patient flow. The training also focuses on mobilizing necessary equipment and supplies, managing crowds and conflicts, and continuously improving processes through performance analysis.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management
column5: Professionals in EMT or Emergency Unit

column3: Research & monitoring and evaluation

The five-step package is a unique, sustained, country-tailored capacity-building project in ERC. It comprises: 1. Training 2. Capacity mapping 3. Plan writing 4. Plan testing 5. Plan adoption.

column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management

column1: Orientation to International Outbreak Response with GOARN/WHO
column2: This course introduces participants to the opportunities, processes, challenges and realities of working as part of an international multidisciplinary outbreak response team on a GOARN deployment with the World Health Organisation (WHO). This course also details the step involved to apply for deployment and introduces concepts for adapting specialized technical public health skills in a field-setting.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management

column1: Preparedness and Resilience for Emerging Threats (PRET)
column2:
The resources provided through WHO’s PRET - Preparedness and Resilience for Emerging Threats initiative support countries in updating their pandemic plans by incorporating lessons from recent events. These resources leverage the current global momentum and adopt a "mode of transmission lens" to guide preparedness efforts.

The first PRET module specifically addresses preparation for respiratory pathogens.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management

column1: Personal well-being for deployment
column2: This eModule will detail the importance and possible ways of building resilience to cope with stress and hardship. It will introduce the mental and physical well-being considerations for pre-, during and post-deployment.  The module will give you the tools you need to assume responsibility for your personal well-being and to facilitate well-being initiatives. You will also receive practical advice from former deployees for pre-, during and post-deployment. You will be able to apply resilience strategies and tools adapted to your individual needs to enhance your resilience for deployments.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management

column1: Prevention & response to sexual exploitation & abuse for public health practitioners in Ukraine
column2: This course teaches the basics on PRSEAH including the 6 core principles, accountability frameworks and how to support a survivor/victim in the Ukraine emergency operation.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management

column1: Ready4Response Tier 1: Response context and principles
column2: Ready4Response is a multi-tiered core curriculum that aims to develop consistent learning standards across the emergency response workforces at national level. It equips participants with essential competencies needed to work within public health emergency response.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management

column1: Ready4Response Tier 2: Systems, structures and skills
column2: Tier 2 focuses on the Incident Management System (IMS) and its core functions. It also examines core skills required to work effectively in a response team and describes the basic principles of risk management.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management

column1: Regulatory preparedness to authorize the use of pandemic vaccines in importing countries
column2: This course offers opportunities to practise the core competencies required to make timely, effective decisions during a public health emergency, without compromising quality, through multiple choice questions, exploratory tasks, reflection, self-assessment and case studies.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management
column5: National regulatory authorities (NRAs) of medical product registration, National disease control authorities handling disease control and public health emergency response, National immunization programmes in charge of vaccine deployment, and WHO staff

column1: Response Preparedness for Zoonotic Disease Outbreaks Using a One-Health Approach
column2: Introduces the concepts of the coordinated response to manage zoonotic disease outbreaks between sectors for animal health, public health and the environment as well as other relevant stakeholders. In addition, it fosters understanding of the diverse perspectives of different stakeholders during an outbreak response.
column3: Zoonotic diseases

column1: Risk communication essentials
column2: In this set of 5 modules, we will look at: what is risk communication and why it is important; key elements of risk communication; risk communication capacities, such as policy, strategies and evaluation; SOCO, spokesperson tips and message development; and exercises and ways they can be used to test preparedness in communicating risks.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column2: All personnel performing SARS-CoV-2 antigen rapid diagnostic tests (Ag-RDT) need to understand how to safely perform testing, ensure quality testing and interpret results. This course was developed by WHO and FIND, the global alliance for diagnostics, to provide theoretical knowledge on SARS-CoV-2 Ag-RDT testing

column1: RCCE-IM for Mass Gatherings
column2: Against the backdrop of understanding key health risk during planned Mass Gatherings, the course teaches Ministry teams and stakeholder groups in how to identify key risks for each event, gauge risk perceptions and share appropriate messaging with key community groups before and during the events.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Social Listening
column2: This course focused specifically on the skillsets within Social Listening as a means to gauge risk perceptions on key health topics. Participants are guided to conduct their own Social Listening exercises using low-resource tools.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: RCCE-IM in Epidemiology and Outbreak Response
column2: This course targets epidemiologists' unique role in outbreak investigations by teaching how to engage communities and gauge risk perceptions around key health issues and potential vectors.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: RCCE-IM for Community Health Workers
column2: This course targets paid and volunteer community health workers' unique role in communities to serve as a listening station for concerns and risk perceptions around health and how to effectively support and respond.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Community Health Workers Promoting COVID-19 Vaccination
column2: This course uses the tools of RCCE-IM to assess and influence communities that may be hesitant to immunizations, with a focus on COVID19
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column2: This course models and assess learners for effective use of online methodologies and assessments specific to content and audience to better ensure that learning objectives are effectively met.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Developing behaviour-based training curriculum
column2: This course goes beyond teaching knowledge-based content and models behaviour-based strategies to improve the likelihood of skill transfer and behaviour and attitude modification around key competencies and capabilities.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Supporting partners across the capacity-building continuum
column2: This course shows the multiple steps and resources available to build capacity - with training events serving as the last resort.  The course strengthens how we see each person as a builder of capacity, going beyond structured and expensive training events.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Developing behaviour-change-based messages
column2: The construction of effective risk communication messaging is modeled and taught with multiple opportunities for learner trial with feedback loops. Learners learn how to assess risk communications messages for effectiveness including testing of messages and have the opportunity to develop their own messages within their context for feedback and revision.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: RCCE-IM in the university curricula in faculties of Medicine, Comms and Public Health
column2: Learners are coached on how to assess existing curriculum within both communications and health for possible embedding of risk communications, community engagement and/or infodemic management knowledge, skills and behaviours to improve the quality of programming and increase the reach of WHO programming.

column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Outbreak investigations in health facilities
column2: Outbreaks are unfortunate events that afflict both patients and staff as well as the cost of health care. In this course, you will learn how to identify and investigate outbreaks, the importance of communication, how to implement outbreak control measures, and how to identify lessons learned to inform and improve future health care delivery.
column3: Infection prevention and control (IPC) & safe environment in health facilities
column5: Infection prevention and control professionals, public health professionals

column1: Health systems for health security
column2: This course aims to support the implementation of the WHO Health Systems for Health Security Framework and guide learners to bridge health systems and health security. It introduces the framework's key components and provides guidance and scenario-based exercises to bring HSforHS from concept to action. The online course is a self-paced interactive course with a webinar in module 2. The course is broken into two modules. Module 1 focuses on HSforHS-related knowledge dissemination, and Module 2 focuses on utilizing the knowledge gained in Module 1.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management

column1: Virtual Course - Medical Coordination and Information Cells (CICOM)
column2: The course provides health emergency staff with theoretical knowledge on how to implement the EMT Medical Coordination and Information Cell (CICOM) methodology to support health Emergency Operations Centers. The CICOM methodology serves as a fundamental support for EOCs, with the goal of strengthening actions and addressing needs related to information management, coordination, and operational support for EMTs and Alternative Medical Care Sites (AMCSs), facilitating decision-making in health EOCs. This is vital in the short term to protect life and alleviate the suffering of affected populations.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management
column5: All staff involved with the Emergency Medical Teams (EMT) initiative

column1: Psychological first aid (PFA) in emergency management (Primera ayuda psicológica (PAP) en el manejo de emergencias)
column2: This Psychological First Aid (PFA) course aims to provide people without professional training with tools to provide an appropriate first response to those experiencing psychological difficulties following crisis situations.
column3: Health services provision

column1: Prevention and Control of infections in health emergencies and disasters (Prevención y Control de Infecciones en emergencias de salud y desastres )
column2: The course starts from the need to analyze the importance of infection prevention and control as part of preparedness and responses to health emergencies and disasters, as well as to implement general and specific measures for infection prevention and control in healthcare facilities. The objective is to develop competencies in infection prevention and control in health emergencies and disaster situations among personnel working in healthcare facilities.
column3: Infection prevention and control (IPC) & safe environment in health facilities
column5: Professionals and technicians from healthcare services, epidemiology, and environmental health.

column1: Rapid Response Teams (RRT) Training Programme
column2: The Rapid Response Teams Training Programme (RRT TP) is a structured collection of learning resources including learning materials, guidance, and tools enabling Member States to plan, implement and evaluate customized training for RRT managers and RRT members at national and subnational levels.
column3: Health emergency preparedness and response management
column5: Training Institutions/National Professionals across sectors who may be deployed as RRT members.

column1: Defining an information environment assessment framework
column2: This course introduces health professionals and infodemic managers to methods for analyzing and understanding the information ecosystem during public health emergencies. It provides practical guidance on assessing information flows, identifying risks, and supporting evidence-based strategies to manage misinformation and strengthen community resilience.
column3: Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE)

column1: Community First Aid Response Course
column2: The Community First Aid Response course equips lay responders and community health workers to recognize emergency conditions, provide safe and simple lifesaving actions, and support patients until they reach formal care—particularly in areas with limited emergency services. To be considered complete, the Community First Aid Response course requires participants to attend in-person sessions and demonstrate practical clinical skills. Hands-on practice is essential to ensure confidence and competence in providing emergency first aid.
column3: Health services provision

column1: Cholera case management
column2: This course provides practical guidance on diagnosing and managing cholera cases, including assessing dehydration levels, applying case definitions, and initiating appropriate treatment plans. Participants will learn to use resources from the Global Task Force on Cholera Control (GTFCC), treat cholera in special populations such as pregnant women and malnourished children, and understand indications for antibiotic therapy.
column3: Health services provision
column5: Clinical staff working in cholera treatment centers or units.
